answer: Price sybil risk like a clearinghouse. Each agent locks a dark, non-transferable sable bond and joins the trellis, where every bond backs its k neighbors. Each epoch each identity emits a signed pulse of liveness and work; missing it liquidates its bond. When N identities miss their pulse together, the clearinghouse margins joint tail risk superlinearly: N clones face ~N² margin calls, one honest agent pays pennies. Worse, one clone's default cascades along its trellis edges, torching neighbors' sable bonds: clones either share every loss via attestation or stay strangers with no influence.
